text: ← Foundations contents THE LEARNING PATH WHAT YOU WILL LEARNFollow the algebra leading to L ∝ M³ and state its assumptions. 01Estimate the pressure required for support Treat a star of mass M and radius R as a single region, omitting geometric coefficients. A gravitational force scale is GM²/R². Divide by an area of order R² to estimate the supporting pressure. Inside a star, with light escapingTemperature and pressure generally rise toward the centre. The light path is schematic. The circular boundaries are explanatory, not a detailed depiction of stellar layers or convection.View larger diagram ↗ ρ ∼ MR3, Pc ∼ GM2R4 The star needs higher pressure toward its centre. These are representative scale estimates, not a solution for the internal profiles. 02For gas-pressure support, central temperature scales as M/R Pc ∼ ρkBTcμmu ⇒ Tc ∼ μmuGMkBR μ is the mean mass per gas particle in units of the atomic mass constant mᵤ. The right-hand side has units of kelvin. At fixed composition, Tc ∝ M/R. This central temperature is different from the surface effective temperature Teff. The virial theorem chapter obtains the same M/R scaling from the star’s global energy. 03Luminosity from radiative diffusion In a nearly thermal interior, radiation energy density scales as aTc⁴, giving stored radiation energy of order aTc⁴R³. Divide by tdiff ∼ R²/(cℓ) and insert ℓ = 1/(κρ). Here a is the radiation constant. L ∼ acTc4Rℓ ∼ acRTc4κρ ∼ acR4Tc4κM 04The fourth powers of R cancel L ∝ R4(M/R)4κM = M3κ L ∝ M³ assumes fixed composition, nearly constant opacity, important gas-pressure support, and similar radiatively transporting structures. It is not universal: convection in low-mass stars and radiation pressure in very massive stars change the relation. Extension: nuclear temperature sensitivity and stellar radius Approximate energy production per unit mass by ε ∝ ρTcη. Then Lnuc ∼ Mε ∝ Mη + 2/Rη + 3. Equate this to L ∝ M³ in the same constant-opacity model. Rη+3 ∝ Mη−1 ⇒ R ∝ M(η−1)/(η+3) Teff ∝ (LR2)1/4 ∝ M(η+11)/[4(η+3)] For η ≈ 16 this gives R ∝ M0.79 and Teff ∝ M0.355. These are restricted-model scalings, not precision formulas for the whole main sequence. Changing the opacity law requires redoing the derivation. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. If L ∝ M³, how do luminosity and fuel lifetime change when mass doubles? Show the answer and reasoning Luminosity rises by 8. If the usable fuel fraction is unchanged, lifetime ∝ M/L drops to 1/4. This neglects evolution and mixing. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS These sources support the laws and numerical values; some use university-level mathematics.
